name: Bruno Mars
description:
'''Peter Gene Hernandez''' (born October 8, 1985), known professionally as '''Bruno Mars''', is an American singer-songwriter, record producer and dancer. Regarded as a [[pop icon]], he is known for his three-octave [[tenor]] vocal range, [[Retro style|retro]] showmanship, musical versatility, and live performances, accompanied by his band, [[Bruno Mars#Band members|the Hooligans]]. Raised in [[Honolulu]], Mars gained recognition in Hawaii as a child for his [[Elvis impersonator|impersonation]] of [[Elvis Presley]], before moving to [[Los Angeles]] in 2003 to pursue a musical career.

Mars established his name in the music industry as a songwriter and co-founder of the production team [[the Smeezingtons]]. He rose to fame as a recording artist after featuring on the US number-one single "[[Nothin' on You]]" (2009) by [[B.o.B]]. Mars's first three studio albums—''[[Doo-Wops & Hooligans]]'' (2010), ''[[Unorthodox Jukebox]]'' (2012), and ''[[24K Magic (album)|24K Magic]]'' (2016)—found critical and commercial success, with the lattermost winning the [[Grammy Award for Album of the Year]]. During the 2010s, Mars achieved further success with the US chart-topping singles: "[[Just the Way You Are (Bruno Mars song)|Just the Way You Are]]", "[[Grenade (song)|Grenade]]", "[[Locked Out of Heaven]]", "[[When I Was Your Man]]", "[[That's What I Like (Bruno Mars song)|That's What I Like]]", and "[[Uptown Funk]]", which became [[Billboard (magazine)|''Billboard'']]{{'s}} [[Billboard Decade-End#2010s|best-performing song of the decade]].

In 2021, Mars released ''[[An Evening with Silk Sonic]]'' alongside [[Anderson .Paak]], as the [[Supergroup (music)|musical superduo]] [[Silk Sonic]]. The album featured the US number-one single "[[Leave the Door Open]]". In 2024, he released two record-breaking number-one duets, "[[Die with a Smile]]" (with [[Lady Gaga]]) and "[[APT. (song)|APT.]]" (with [[Rosé (singer)|Rosé]]). His first solo album in ten years, ''[[The Romantic (album)|The Romantic]]'' (2026), was led by the global chart-toppers "[[I Just Might]]" and "[[Risk It All (Bruno Mars song)|Risk It All]]".

Mars has sold over 150 million records worldwide, making him one of the [[List of best-selling music artists|best-selling music artists of all time]]. He amassed [[Artists with the most number-ones on the Billboard Hot 100 chart|ten number-one singles]] on the ''Billboard'' Hot 100 and spent a record 31 weeks atop the [[Billboard Global 200|''Billboard'' Global 200]]. Mars is the only artist to surpass [[List of most-streamed artists on Spotify|150 million monthly listeners]] on [[Spotify]] and the first to receive six diamond-[[RIAA certification|certified]] songs by the [[Recording Industry Association of America]] (RIAA). Mars's [[List of awards and nominations received by Bruno Mars|accolades]] include 16 [[Grammy Award]]s, 17 [[American Music Awards]], 9 [[Billboard Music Awards|''Billboard'' Music Awards]], 5 [[Brit Awards]], 7 [[MTV Video Music Awards]] and 14 [[Soul Train Awards]]. ''[[Time (magazine)|Time]]'' named him among the [[Time 100|100 most influential people in the world]] in 2011.
